input.text: In Colorado branches, accounts open fewer than 60 days are new accounts for hold and limit purposes.
input.heading: Colorado requirements

input.text: In Colorado branches, account records are kept for 5 years after the account closes.
input.heading: Colorado requirements

input.text: In Kansas branches, customers have 30 days from the statement date to dispute a debit card transaction.
input.heading: Kansas requirements

input.text: In Kansas branches, complaints should be closed within 30 business days of the day they arrive.
input.heading: Kansas requirements

input.text: In Oklahoma branches, vault combinations are changed every 12 months and whenever an employee who knows the combination leaves.
input.heading: Oklahoma requirements

input.text: In Oklahoma branches, mail the customer a notice at least 60 days before the account is classified as dormant.
input.heading: Oklahoma requirements

input.text: In Texas branches, dormant accounts are charged a maintenance fee of $3 per month.
input.heading: Texas requirements

input.text: In Texas branches, refer an account for charge-off once it has been negative for 60 days.
input.heading: Texas requirements

input.text: Change the vault combination at least every 3 months.
input.heading: What branches need to know
